extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory and procedural requirements for preparing and filing United States patent applications (including provisional applications), covering specification, claims, drawings, oath/declaration, inventorship, filing date, abandonment, and priority/benefit rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written application by inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent shall be made, or authorized to be made, by the inventor, except as otherwise provided in this title, in writing to the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability noted for different date ranges (AIA, pre-AIA, pre-PLT) in the source; the basic requirement is a written application made or authorized by the inventor to the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of application
rubrics_metrics.description: Such application shall include—(A) a specification as prescribed by section 112; (B) a drawing as prescribed by section 113; and (C) an oath or declaration as prescribed by section 115.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification, drawings, and oath/declaration are required elements. Specifics of each are governed by the referenced sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee, oath/declaration, and claims may be later within prescribed period
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee, oath or declaration, and 1 or more claims may be submitted after the filing date of the application, within such period and under such conditions, including the payment of a surcharge, as may be prescribed by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee, oath/declaration, or claims are not submitted within the Director-prescribed period (including any surcharge), the application shall be regarded as abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of an application shall be the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is critical for priority and statutorily defined filing-date rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application: authorization and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application for patent shall be made or authorized to be made by the inventor ... in writing to the Director. Such application shall include—(A) a specification as prescribed by section 112(a); and (B) a drawing as prescribed by section 113.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications are filed by the inventor in writing and must include the specification (per 112(a)) and drawings (per 113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application: claim not required
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim, as required by subsections (b) through (e) of section 112, shall not be required in a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications may lack claims; however, they do not obtain certain benefits (see separate criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application fee rules and abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be accompanied by the fee required by law. The fee may be submitted after the filing date of the application, within such period and under such conditions ... Upon failure to submit the fee within such prescribed period, the application shall be regarded as abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may allow fee submission after filing within prescribed period (possibly with surcharge). Failure leads to abandonment of provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a provisional application shall be the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors filing-date rule for non-provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application abandonment after 12 months and treatment as nonprovisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding the absence of a claim, upon timely request and as prescribed by the Director, a provisional application may be treated as an application filed under subsection (a). ... if no such request is made, the provisional application shall be regarded as abandoned 12 months after the filing date of such application and shall not be subject to revival after such 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional is ordinarily abandoned after 12 months unless timely converted/treated as a nonprovisional as prescribed by the Director; no revival after 12 months if abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional applications: no right of priority or benefit of earlier filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application shall not be entitled to the right of priority of any other application under section 119, 365(a), or 386(a) or to the benefit of an earlier filing date in the United States under section 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications generally do not confer the statutory priority/benefit rights listed; exceptions are governed by statute/regulation (see Director-prescribed rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional applications: applicable provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this title relating to applications for patent shall apply to provisional applications for patent, except as otherwise provided, and except that provisional applications for patent shall not be subject to sections 131 and 135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most application rules apply to provisionals, but not sections 131 (ex parte examination?) and 135 (reissue?) as specified — check statute for exact section meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior filed application may constitute specification/drawings for filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may prescribe the conditions ... under which a reference made upon the filing of an application under subsection (a) to a previously filed application ... shall constitute the specification and any drawings of the subsequent application for purposes of a filing date. A copy of the specification and any drawings of the previously filed application shall be submitted within such period and under such conditions as may be prescribed by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the required copy of the previous application's specification/drawings is not submitted within the prescribed period the subsequent application will be regarded as abandoned and may be treated as never filed unless revived under section 27 and the copy submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification written-description and enablement requirement (35 U.S.C. 112(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification shall contain a written description of the invention, and of the manner and process of making and using it, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use the same, and shall set forth the best mode contemplated by the inventor or joint inventor of carrying out the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory written-description, enablement, and best-mode requirement—used to assess sufficiency of disclosure to one skilled in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention (35 U.S.C. 112(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification shall conclude with one or more claims particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims define the metes and bounds of the invention; claim drafting must satisfy the statutory 'particularly point out and distinctly claim' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim forms: independent, dependent, and multiple dependent (35 U.S.C. 112(c)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim may be written in independent or, if the nature of the case admits, in dependent or multiple dependent form. A dependent claim shall contain a reference to a claim previously set forth and then specify a further limitation ... A multiple dependent claim shall contain a reference, in the alternative only, to more than one claim previously set forth ... A multiple dependent claim shall not serve as a basis for any other multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims incorporate all limitations of the claim(s) to which they refer. Multiple dependent claims must reference in the alternative and cannot be bases for other multiple dependent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-or-step plus-function claiming (35 U.S.C. 112(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An element in a claim for a combination may be expressed as a means or step for performing a specified function without the recital of structure, material, or acts in support thereof, and such claim shall be construed to cover the corresponding structure, material, or acts described in the specification and equivalents thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means-plus-function claim elements are construed to the corresponding structure/material/acts disclosed in the spec and equivalents—drafting/analysis must account for this limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings where necessary (35 U.S.C. 113)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall furnish a drawing where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter sought to be patented. When the nature of such subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing and the applicant has not furnished such a drawing, the Director may require its submission within a time period of not less than two months from the sending of a notice thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings submitted after the filing date may not be used to overcome any insufficiency of the specification due to lack of an enabling disclosure or otherwise inadequate disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models and specimens may be required (35 U.S.C. 114)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may require the applicant to furnish a model of convenient size to exhibit advantageously the several parts of his invention. When the invention relates to a composition of matter, the Director may require the applicant to furnish specimens or ingredients for the purpose of inspection or experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of models/specimens is at Director's discretion for inspection/experimentation; models may help understanding but are not generally required except when prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath or declaration: naming and execution (35 U.S.C. 115(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent ... shall include, or be amended to include, the name of the inventor for any invention claimed in the application. Except as otherwise provided in this section, each individual who is the inventor or a joint inventor of a claimed invention in an application for patent shall execute an oath or declaration in connection with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each inventor named for a claimed invention must execute the required oath/declaration unless an exception or substitute statement applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statements in oath/declaration (35 U.S.C. 115(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration ... shall contain statements that—(1) the application was made or was authorized to be made by the affiant or declarant; and (2) such individual believes himself or herself to be the original inventor or an original joint inventor of a claimed invention in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration must affirm authorship/authorization and belief in original inventorship; false statements carry penalties (see separate criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may require additional information in oath/declaration (35 U.S.C. 115(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may specify additional information relating to the inventor and the invention that is required to be included in an oath or declaration under subsection (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath/declaration content can be expanded by Director regulation as necessary for administrative processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement permitted in lieu of oath/declaration (35 U.S.C. 115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of executing an oath or declaration under subsection (a), the applicant for patent may provide a substitute statement ... permitted with respect to any individual who—(A) is unable to file the oath or declaration because the individual—(i) is deceased; (ii) is under legal incapacity; or (iii) cannot be found or reached after diligent effort; or (B) is under an obligation to assign the invention but has refused to make the oath or declaration required under subsection (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute statements are specifically allowed for listed circumstances; Director may specify additional permitted circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of substitute statement (35 U.S.C. 115(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement ... shall—(A) identify the individual with respect to whom the statement applies; (B) set forth the circumstances representing the permitted basis for the filing of the substitute statement in lieu of the oath or declaration under subsection (a); and (C) contain any additional information, including any showing, required by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute statements must identify the inventor and explain the ground for substitution and provide any additional Director-required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements in assignment may satisfy oath/declaration requirement (35 U.S.C. 115(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who is under an obligation of assignment of an application for patent may include the required statements under subsections (b) and (c) in the assignment executed by the individual, in lieu of filing such statements separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements required in oath/declaration may be placed in the assignment document instead, if properly executed and recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing oath/declaration/substitute/assignment (35 U.S.C. 115(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant for patent shall provide each required oath or declaration under subsection (a), substitute statement under subsection (d), or recorded assignment meeting the requirements of subsection (e) no later than the date on which the issue fee for the patent is paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required inventor statements or substitute statements must be on file no later than payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier-filed application containing required statements may relieve later filing (35 U.S.C. 115(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements under this section shall not apply to an individual with respect to an application for patent ... if—(A) an oath or declaration meeting the requirements of subsection (a) was executed by the individual and was filed in connection with the earlier-filed application; (B) a substitute statement meeting the requirements of subsection (d) was filed in connection with the earlier filed application; or (C) an assignment meeting the requirements of subsection (e) was executed ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required statements were properly filed in an earlier application from which benefit is claimed, they may satisfy the later application's requirements; Director may still require copies of those earlier-filed documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental and corrected statements; savings clause (35 U.S.C. 115(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person making a statement required under this section may withdraw, replace, or otherwise correct the statement at any time. ... A patent shall not be invalid or unenforceable based upon the failure to comply with a requirement under this section if the failure is remedied as provided under paragraph (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may correct or replace required statements; failure to comply does not automatically invalidate a patent if remedied per the statute/regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of penalties for willful false statements (35 U.S.C. 115(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any declaration or statement filed pursuant to this section shall contain an acknowledgment that any willful false statement made in such declaration or statement is punishable under section 1001 of title 18 by fine or imprisonment of not more than 5 years, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarations must include explicit acknowledgment of criminal penalties for willful false statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventions: filing and oath rules (35 U.S.C. 116(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an invention is made by two or more persons jointly, they shall apply for patent jointly and each make the required oath, except as otherwise provided in this title. Inventors may apply for a patent jointly even though (1) they did not physically work together or at the same time, (2) each did not make the same type or amount of contribution, or (3) each did not make a contribution to the subject matter of every claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint inventorship has a broad scope; co-inventors can apply jointly despite differing contributions or timing of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omitted inventor procedures (35 U.S.C. 116(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a joint inventor refuses to join in an application for patent or cannot be found or reached after diligent effort, the application may be made by the other inventor on behalf of himself and the omitted inventor. The Director, on proof of the pertinent facts and after such notice to the omitted inventor as he prescribes, may grant a patent to the inventor making the application, subject to the same rights which the omitted inventor would have had if he had been joined. The omitted inventor may subsequently join in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes exist to file when a joint inventor is unwilling or unavailable; Director may grant subject to omitted inventor's rights and allow later joinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship errors (35 U.S.C. 116(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever through error a person is named in an application for patent as the inventor, or through an error an inventor is not named in an application, the Director may permit the application to be amended accordingly, under such terms as he prescribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director-authorized amendments can correct erroneous inventor naming under prescribed terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death or incapacity of inventor (35 U.S.C. 117)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal representatives of deceased inventors and of those under legal incapacity may make application for patent upon compliance with the requirements and on the same terms and conditions applicable to the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal representatives can file to preserve rights for deceased or incapacitated inventors subject to the same requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by other than inventor (assignees/agents) (35 U.S.C. 118)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person to whom the inventor has assigned or is under an obligation to assign the invention may make an application for patent. A person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter may make an application for patent on behalf of and as agent for the inventor on proof of the pertinent facts and a showing that such action is appropriate to preserve the rights of the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Director grants a patent on an application filed by a person other than the inventor, the patent shall be granted to the real party in interest and upon such notice to the inventor as the Director considers to be sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit of earlier filing date; right of priority (35 U.S.C. 119) (introductory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit of earlier filing date; right of priority (35 U.S.C. 119(a) as set forth is only applicable to patent applications subject to the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 119 covers entitlement to benefit of earlier foreign/other filings and priority rights; details and conditions are set out in the statute (the chunk introduces 119 but full subsections follow elsewhere).
